rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem argues that a mother's pregnancy, sleepless care, feeding, and self-sacrifice make her right immense and repayment small.
rows.anchor: لأمك حق لو علمت كبير كثيرك ياهذا لديه يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view defines commanded gratitude as obedience and pleasing acts: prayer and fasting toward God, and kinship and dutifulness toward parents.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو الطاعة وفعل ما يرضي كالصلاة والصيام بالنسبة إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan says the five daily prayers express gratitude to God, while supplicating for one's parents after them expresses gratitude to them.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان بن عيينة من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi treats Sufyan's statement as an illustration of some forms of gratitude, not an exhaustive definition.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذا بيان لبعض أفراد الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God explains why the command must be obeyed: people return to Him, and He repays their disobedience.
rows.anchor: إلي المصير 41 تعليل لوجوب الامتثال بالأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the most complete practical worship and completes the son's self after belief; the affectionate address seeks to incline him to obey.
rows.anchor: الصلاة التي هي أكمل العبادات تكميلا من حيث العمل بعد تكميله من حيث الاعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has the father tell his son to pray promptly when its time comes, rest through fulfilling the obligation, and pray in congregation even atop a spearhead.
rows.anchor: يا بني إذا جاء وقت الصلاة فلا تؤخرها لشيء صلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong completes others; the commands do not refer to one specified good or evil.
rows.anchor: تكميلا لغيرك والظاهر أنه ليس المراد معروفا ونكرا معينين

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets the good to be enjoined as monotheism and the wrong to be forbidden as associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: عن إبن جبير أنه قال : وأمر بالمعروف يعني التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is needed for hardships generally, especially the burdens of prayer and the opposition encountered when enjoining right and forbidding wrong; prayer can be arduous.
rows.anchor: من الشدائد والمحن لا سيما فيما أمرت به من إقامة الصلاة والأمر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr narrows the patience command to harm and hardship suffered while enjoining right or forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: وقال إبن جبير : وأصبر على ما أصابك في أمر الأمر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr takes “that” to refer specifically to patience in the face of such harm; Alusi notes the singular demonstrative suits this reading.
rows.anchor: عند إبن جبير وهو يناسب أفراد أسم الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “that” points to patience together with the other commands, with the singular construed by interpreting the referent as a unified matter.
rows.anchor: أو الإشارة إلى الصبر وإلى سائر ما أمر به والإفراد للتأويل بما ذكر

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits the interpretation that “among the resolute matters” means matters God has decisively imposed as obligatory.
rows.anchor: وروى ذلك عن إبن جريج والعزم بهذا المعنى مما ينسب إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that interpretation, ʿazm is used for the thing resolved upon, and the construction makes the attribute qualify the described matters.
rows.anchor: والمراد به هنا المعزوم إطلاقا للمصدر على المفعول والإضافة من إضافة الصفة إلى الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A grammatical alternative takes ʿazm as an active participle, “resolute matters,” through figurative attribution rather than an “in” genitive.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون العزم بمعنى الفاعل أي عازم الأمور من عزم الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view understands the phrase as noble morals and the firm resolves of prudent people following the path of salvation; Abu Hayyan prefers obligatory matters.
rows.anchor: من مكارم الأخلاق وعزائم أهل الحزم السالكين طريق النجاة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says ʿazm is ḥazm in Hudhayl's dialect, but Alusi rejects his suggestion that one word arose by changing the other’s initial consonant.
rows.anchor: وما قاله المبرد من أن العين قلبت جاء ليس بشيء لإطراد تصاريف كل من اللفظين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause gives the reason for obeying the preceding commands and emphasizes their special importance.
rows.anchor: والجملة تعليل لوجوب الامتثال بما سبق وفيه اعتناء بشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing punishment for disobedience and reward for obedience to God and the Messenger, the passage magnifies the weight and difficulty of religious duties by parable, while indicating acceptance and refusal were voluntary.
rows.anchor: عظم شأن ما يوجبها من التكاليف الشرعية وصعوبة أمرها بطريق التمثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amanah, a verbal noun related to security and trust, depicts duties as rights God entrusted to accountable beings, requiring willing obedience, careful preservation, and complete delivery.
rows.anchor: وهي في الأصل مصدر كالأمن والأمان تنبيها على أنها حقوق مرعية أودعها الله تعالى المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the duty an offer to the heavens, earth, and mountains represents assessing their particular capacities and stresses solicitude and desire for their acceptance.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن اعتبارها بالنسبة إلى استعداد ما ذكر من السموات وغيرها من حيث الخصوصيات بالعرض عليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their refusal and fear represent their incapacity and the duty's incompatibility with their nature, heightening its gravity; carrying it represents its heaviness.
rows.anchor: وعن عدم استعدادهن لقبولها ومنافاتها لما هن عليه بالإباء والإشفاق منها لتهويل أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counterfactual means that if these mighty bodies had consciousness and were charged with the trust, they would refuse and fear it; the wording presents the supposition as fact to make the point vivid.
rows.anchor: لو كلفت هاتيك الأجرام العظام التي هي مثل في القوة والشدة مراعاتها وكانت ذات شعور وإدراك لأبين قبولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” means the human species, as in the verses describing humanity as ungrateful and transgressive; bearing the trust means readiness to accept it or undertaking it at the primordial covenant despite frailty.
rows.anchor: وحملها الإنسان ( أي هذا الجنس نحو ( إن الإنسان لربه لكنود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity may have accepted through its innate capacity or through a spoken pledge on the day of the covenant; humans are singled out although jinn are also accountable, since angels face no hardship contrary to their nature.
rows.anchor: بتكليفه إياها يوم الميثاق أي تكلفها والتزمها مع ما فيه من ضعف البنية ورخاوة القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that humanity is unjust and ignorant interrupts the account to foreshadow failure and answer possible doubt; it describes the majority who violate their original nature or pledge, not those who preserve God's nature-given disposition.
rows.anchor: اعتراض وسط بين الحمل وغايته للإيذان من أول الأمر بعدم وفائه بما تحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is told to exhort believers to piety and convey the command in God's own words, honoring them by calling them His servants and strengthening the command's force.
rows.anchor: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يذكر المؤمنين ويحملهم على التقوى والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to those who do good explains the command or its binding force; “good” is indefinite for magnification, and the good promised is Paradise in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب الامتثال به والجار والمجرور متعلق بمحذوف هو خبر مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “in this world” modifies doing good, while “good” is an emphatic indefinite subject; the earth's breadth is an aside removing lack of opportunity in one's homeland as an excuse for neglect.
rows.anchor: في هذه الدنيا متعلق بأحسنوا واسم الإشارة للإحضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the patient continues the parenthetical explanation, contrasting the promised good with the special unlimited recompense of patience.
rows.anchor: إنما يوفى الصابرون أجورهم بغير حساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aside explains that those unable to obey properly in their homeland should move elsewhere and migrate toward God for His approval; in that cause, every hardship is outweighed by its reward.
rows.anchor: فليتحولوا إن لم يتمكنوا عنها وليهاجروا إلى ربهم لنيل الرضوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised special recompense answers whether migrants and those able to obey at home are equal: patient migrants forsake attachments and follow prophets and the righteous, receiving immeasurable reward.
rows.anchor: الذين صبروا على الهجرة ومفارقة المحاب والاقتداء بالأنبياء والصالحين أجرهم بغير حساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to passive voice stresses patience as the cause of reward and implies the addressees will likewise be repaid for their patience, as earlier people were.
rows.anchor: وعدل عنه إلى المنزل تنبيها على أن المقتضى لذلك صبرهم فيفيد أنكم توفون أجوركم بصبركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although prompted here by migration, patience and the unrestricted recompense cover every affliction; “without reckoning” can modify the reward or the patient people and is primarily hyperbole for abundance.
rows.anchor: وهو محمول على العموم شامل للصبر على كل بلاء غير مخصوص بالصبر على المهاجرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains reward without reckoning as so abundant that no accountant can reach or comprehend its measure.
rows.anchor: قول ابن عباس لا يهتدي إليه حساب الحساب ولا يعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A less immediate grammatical possibility makes “without reckoning” describe the patient people: they are not reckoned at all, though the apparent sense is abundant reward.
rows.anchor: وجوز جعل الحال من الصابرين على معنى لا يحاسبون أصلا والمتبادر ما يفيد المبالغة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi links “in this world” semantically to “good,” rather than to doing good.
rows.anchor: عن السدي أن قوله تعالى ( في الدنيا ) متعلق بحسنة من حيث المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi notes grammatical objections to treating the phrase as a circumstantial modifier of the indefinite subject “good”; making it a subject governed by the adverb only works on al-Akhfash's weak position.
rows.anchor: ورد بأنها مبتدأ ولا يجوز الحال منه على الصحيح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads “in this world” as an explanatory gloss for “good”: the good is health and well-being in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : هو بيان لحسنة والتقدير هي في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the explanatory reading suits the meaning better than a restrictive circumstantial reading: worldly health is a small immediate benefit, while full recompense comes in the next life.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشف : وإنما آثر كونه بيانا مع جواز كونه حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that alternative, the earth's breadth removes objections based on differing climates and bodily conditions; worldly health is an immediate share, whereas full limitless reward belongs to the patient, consoling sufferers and encouraging worship and obedience.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك تسلية لأهل البلاء وتنشيط للعباد على مكابدة العبادات وتحريض على ملازمة الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi calls the alternative fine but prefers the primary reading: the context more directly removes inability to obey at home as an excuse.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن الإعتراض لإزاحة العلة في التفريط أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary reading also matches Quranic injunctions to migrate when God's earth is constricted, and normally a prepositional phrase attaches to the closest suitable expression absent a contrary reason.
rows.anchor: من نحو ( ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further objection to the health reading is that worldly health can benefit unbelievers too; calling it divine entrapment is unconvincing given the verse about people claiming worldly good as their due.
rows.anchor: فإن الحسنة بذلك المعنى في شأن المخالفين أتم والقول بأنها استدراج في شأنهم لا حسنة ليس بالظاهر

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi transmits al-Suddi's gloss of worldly good as good reputation and favorable mention, as well as health and safety.
rows.anchor: والذي نقله الطبرسي عن السدي تفسير الحسنة في الدنيا بالثناء الحسن والذكر الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the promised good as God's guardianship, which unbelievers do not share.
rows.anchor: وفسرها بعضهم بولاية الله تعالى وعليه فليس للمخالفين منها نصيب

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says God's earth here means Medina; on that view, doing good means emigrating and the worldly good is relief from enemies.
rows.anchor: فعن عطاء أرض الله تعالى المدينة قال أبو حيان : فعلى هذا يكون

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim allows “God's earth” to mean Paradise, supporting the reading that the good of the next life is eternal residence there.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : لا يمتنع ذلك لأنه تعالى أمر المؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the interpretation of God's earth as Paradise arbitrary and unsupported.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه ابن عطية بأنه تحكم لا دليل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers the first interpretation: “good” includes good things in both worldly and next life, while ihsan means inward and outward good action.
rows.anchor: والرجحان لما سمعت أولا واختير فيه شمول الحسنة لحسنات الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan is worshipping God as if seeing Him, or at least knowing He sees the worshipper, according to the Prophet's explanation in the Gabriel report.
rows.anchor: في حديث جبريل عليه السلام أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some transmitted accounts say the verse was revealed about Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib and his companions when they resolved to migrate to Abyssinia.
rows.anchor: والآية على ما في بعض الآثار نزلت في جعفر بن أبي طالب وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse highlights the great merit of those who remain patient.
rows.anchor: وفيها من الدلالة على فضل الصابرين ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The independent sentence encourages the Messenger to endure polytheist abuse and answer harm with good; generally, good and evil deeds differ in effects and rulings.
rows.anchor: سيقت لبيان محاسن الأعمال الجارية بين العباد أثر بيان محاسن الأعمال الجارية بين العبد والرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second negative particle is extra for emphasis, as in the verse denying equality of shade and heat.
rows.anchor: الثانية مزيدة لتأكيد النفي مثلها في قوله تعالى ( ولا الظل ولا الحرور )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repel any evil from an enemy with a better response, such as doing good to an offender, which surpasses merely forgiving; “better” has a general omitted comparator.
rows.anchor: ادفع السيئة حيث اعترضك من بعض أعاديك بالتي هي أحسن منها وهي الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “better” instead of simply “good” signals that lesser goodness will then be easy; the question-and-answer form stresses that this is a matter to ask and heed.
rows.anchor: عن سؤال من قال : كيف أصنع للمبالغة والإشارة إلى أنه مهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the good and evil are not two particular acts; the authorial reading is a general moral instruction.
rows.anchor: ومما ذكرنا يعلم أن ليس المراد بالحسنة والسيئة أمرين معينين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali interprets the good as love for the Messenger and his family, and the evil as hatred of them.
rows.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه حب الرسول وآله عليهم الصلاة والسلام والسيئة بغضهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the good as the declaration that there is no god but God and the evil as associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الحسنة لا إله إلا الله والسيئة الشرك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets the terms as the two invitations to monotheism and associationism.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : الدعوتان إليهما وقال الضحاك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reads the contrast as forbearance versus obscenity.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : الحلم والفحش وقيل : الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported glosses include patience and leniency versus harshness; Alusi doubts some are intended here or reliably transmitted from their named authorities.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى أن بعض المروي يكاد لا تصح إرادته هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second grammatical reading takes both terms as generic classes whose individual deeds vary from good to better and evil to worse; the second la then is not extra, and the command means answer the worse evil with the best good.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد بيان تفاوت الحسنات والسيئات في أنفسهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded response can make a hostile person resemble a compassionate friend.
rows.anchor: بيان لنتيجة الدفع المأمور به فإذا فعلت ذلك صار عدوك المشاق مثل الولي الشفيق

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the simile is necessary because answering well often makes an enemy appear friendly without turning him into a true intimate.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : دخلت ( كأن ) المفيدة للتشبيه لأن العدو لا يعود وليا حميما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says this may state only the usual minimum result; sometimes good responses dissolve hostility altogether, as an anonymous verse says.
rows.anchor: وإلا فقد تزول العداوة بالكلية بذلك كما قيل إن العداوة تستحيل مودة بتدارك الفهوات بالحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording the one between you and whom there is enmity is more expressive than your enemy, though longer, and so was rhetorically chosen.
rows.anchor: أبلغ من عدوك ولذا اختير عليه مع اختصاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the verse was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan, once the Messenger enemy and later a close friend to Sunnis; Alusi adds a sharp aside about his grandson Yazid.
rows.anchor: فصار عند أهل السنة وليا مصافيا وكأن ما عنده انتقل إلى ولد ولده يزيد عليه من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the noble act of answering evil with the best response, understood from context; it may alternatively refer to the best response itself.
rows.anchor: أي ما يلقى ويؤتى هذه الفعلة والخصلة الشريفة التي هي الدفع بالتي هي أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted but unpersuasive interpretation makes the pronoun refer to the testimony that there is no god but God, by construing it as the best response; another says it means Paradise, which Alusi dismisses.
rows.anchor: وحكى محكي أن الضمير لشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله فكأنه أرجع للتي هي أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talha and Ibn Kathir in one transmission read the verb as “meets” rather than “is granted.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة وابن كثير في رواية ( وما يلاقاها )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person of great fortune has excellent traits and a perfected soul; on this reading the clause praises the person.
rows.anchor: ذو نصيب عظيم من خصال الخير وكمال النفس كما روي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the great fortune is a great reward, making the clause a promise; another view says it is Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : ذو حظ عظيم من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “is granted” reinforces praise of this eminent moral act.
rows.anchor: تلك الفعلة الجليلة ولأوحد أهل عصره

rows.speaker: صالح أفندي
rows.claim: Salih Efendi offers a logical wordplay: the two universal premises yield that every patient person has great fortune, a positive universal conclusion; this lets the patient recognize his good lot and remain within patience.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : ( وما يلقاها إلا الذين صبروا ) الآية يمكن أن يؤخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reconstructs the wordplay as a first-figure syllogism: every patient person receives the act, and everyone receiving it has great fortune; the positive universal conclusion is the noblest categorical form.
rows.anchor: كل صابر هو الذي يلقاها وكل من يلقاها فهو ذو حظ عظيم ينتج كل صابر هو ذو حظ عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “deep” state is profound ignorance that envelops people like water covering what lies within it; heedlessness means being inattentive to what they were commanded, broadly any negligence.
rows.anchor: غافلون عما أمروا به فالمراد بالسهو مطلق الغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Likewise” resumes and emphasizes the matter after intervening discussion: earlier and present rejecters speak alike about the Messenger, restating the earlier description of their discordant talk.
rows.anchor: بعد أن تقدمت عموماأو خصوصا في قوله تعالى ( إنكم لفي قول مختلف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Likewise” is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning “the matter is so”; it points forward to the statement about earlier peoples and their accusations.
rows.anchor: الأمر كذلك أي مثل ما يذكر ويأتيك خبره إشارة إلى الكلام الذي يتلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects attaching “likewise” to the verb under the scope of the negative particle, or to the following speech verb; neither construction is licensed by the syntax.
rows.anchor: ولا يجو نصبه بأتى على أنه صفة لمصدره والإشارة إلى الإتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before them” refers to Quraysh's predecessors, and “a messenger” means any messenger sent by God, whom they accused of sorcery or madness.
rows.anchor: وضمير قبلهم لقريش أي ما أتى الذين من قبل قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusation may be construed as a predicate (“he is a sorcerer”) or as two quoted alternatives; in al-Bahr, “or” divides speakers: some said sorcerer, others madman, and some both.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر هي للتفصيل أي قال بعض : ساحر وقال بعض مجنون

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: In response to the claim that every messenger was rejected, al-Razi says law-preserving prophets such as Joshua were prophets following an earlier messenger, not messengers themselves.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الإمام بقوله : لا نسلم أن المقرر رسول بل هو نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi notes reports and verses indicate that law-preserving prophets were also called messengers, and this answer still leaves Adam, who was sent but not accused.
rows.anchor: وتعقب الأخبار وكذا الآيات دالة على أن المقررين رسل وأيضا يبقى الاستشكال بآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer limits the verse to messengers who came directly to an existing people with a message; it excludes those who only reaffirmed an earlier law, and Adam had no community beyond Eve.
rows.anchor: المتبادر من إتيان الرسول قوما مجيئه إياهم مع عدم تبليغ غيره إياهم ما أتى به من قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal restricts “messenger” to descendants of Adam, thereby excluding Adam himself, but Alusi also records objections to the explanation.
rows.anchor: إن المراد من رسول من بني آدم فلا يدخل هو عليه السلام في ذلك

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Razi answers that a plural attribution can mean most people rather than every individual; mentioning rejecters alone serves the passage's consolatory purpose.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الإمام بأن إسناد القول إلى ضمير الجمع إرادة الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some use the majority reading to solve the earlier objections too, but Alusi finds that reply weak; reading “those before them” as unbelievers is also unconvincing, and he urges further reflection.
rows.anchor: وحمل بعضهم الذين منقبلهم على الكفار ودفع به الاستشكالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question marvels that earlier and later rejecters all used the same vile accusation, as if they had advised each other to say it.
rows.anchor: تعجيب من إجماعهم على تلك الكلمة الشنيعة أي كأن الأولين والآخرين منهم أوصى بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question denies that they ever conspired together to say it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنكار للتواصي أي ما تواصوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “rather” clause redirects from shared counsel to their actual common cause: participation in transgression that drives the accusation.
rows.anchor: إضراب عن أن التواصي جامعهم إلى أن الجامع لهم على ذلك القول مشاركتهم في الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky was created raised from the start, not first low and then lifted; the primary sense is physical elevation, though it can also include its rank as the source of divine decrees, commands, and angelic presence.
rows.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة ابتداءا لا أنها كانت مخفوضة ورفعها والظاهر أن المراد برفعها الرفع الصوري

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads “the sky” in the nominative as the subject of a nominal clause coordinated with the preceding nominal clause.
rows.anchor: وقراأبو السمال ( والسماء ) بالرفع على الأبتداء ولا إشكال فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading implies an elided verb, “He raises the sky”; attaching it to the larger clause about stars and trees creates an undesirable mismatch of nominal and verbal clauses.
rows.anchor: السماء فتكون الجملة فعلية فإن عطفت على جملة النجم والشجر يسجدان

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali attaches the phrase to the smaller clause about the stars and trees, arguing that a conjunct need not preserve its counterpart's grammatical form.
rows.anchor: لا يلزم في المعطوف على الشيء أن يعتبر فيه حال ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians prefer the larger attachment, allowing the contrast because it carries a rhetorical point; al-Tibi favors coordination with the sun and moon clause to distinguish continued subjection from emphasis.
rows.anchor: قال الطيبي : الظاهر أن يعطف على جملة ( الشمس والقمر بحسبان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi also notes the broader grammatical question of coordinating onto a clause that itself has both nominal and verbal faces.
rows.anchor: والكلام فيما يتعلق بالرفع والنصب فيما إذا ولي العاطف جملة ذات وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Setting the balance means instituting and commanding justice: giving each deserving recipient their due and every right its fulfillment orders and stabilizes the world.
rows.anchor: شرع العدل وأمر به بأن وفر على كل مستعد مستحقه ووفى في كل ذي حق حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying states that the heavens and earth stand through justice; some interpret this as referring only to their inhabitants, but Alusi prefers the entire created order.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : بالعدل قامت السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects limiting the Prophetic statement to adjudication between people: it means God's justice in giving each thing its created form and due.
rows.anchor: بل المراد به عدل الله عز وجل وإعطاؤه سبحانه كل شيء خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Tabari, and most interpreters take the balance as a metaphor for justice; Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak take it as the known measuring device and similar instruments.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الميزان بما ذكر هو المروي عن مجاهد والطبري والأكثرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the instrument reading, the balance is placed on earth for human affairs, judgments, and the commanded fairness of giving and taking; the term may be figurative, literal, or a name for any means of measuring.
rows.anchor: والضحاك أن المرادبه ما يعرف به مقادير الأشياء من الآلة المعروفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The physical balance reading better fits the following command and forms a contrast with the sky's raising; Alusi nevertheless prefers the justice reading as more comprehensive and beneficial.
rows.anchor: ورجح القولان الأخيران بأن ما بعد أشد ملاءمة لهما وبين الوضع والرفع عليهما تقابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abdullah's reading has “and lowered the balance.”
rows.anchor: وقد قرأعبد الله وخفض الميزان والأول بانه أتم فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to perform weighing justly; al-Raghib broadens it to fairness in all human actions and speech.
rows.anchor: قوموا وزنكم بالعدل وقال الراغب : هذا إشارة إلى مراعاة المعدلة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says to level the balance's beam when buying and selling; Sufyan ibn Uyayna says fairness is enacted by the hand and grounded in the heart.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهدأن المعنى أقيموا لسان الميزان بالعدل إذا أردتم الأخذ والإعطاء

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says the balance is set correctly by the hand, while equity resides in the heart.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة : الإقامة باليد والقسط بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command coordinates with the preceding negated clause despite its imperative form, since it can be read as a verbal noun; another makes the earlier la prohibitive for parallelism.
rows.anchor: ولا يضر في ذلك كونها إنشائية وتلك خبرية لأنها لتأويلها بالمفرد تجردت عن معنى الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not reduce the balance: its proper function is to make measurements equal; repeating the word reinforces the instruction and urge to use it.
rows.anchor: أي لا تنقصوه فإن منحقه أن يسوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several readings vary the vowels of the verb “reduce”; Zayd ibn Ali and Bilal ibn Abi Burda read with an open first vowel and kasra on the sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأزيد بن علي وبلال بن أبي بردة بفتح التاء وكسر السين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari analyzes a reading as originally requiring a preposition that was deleted; Abu Hayyan objects that the verb is independently transitive, so deletion is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وخرج ذلك الزمخشري على أن الأصل ولا تخسروا في الميزان فحذف الجار

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the verb can take an object directly, citing Quranic usage, so there is no need to posit a deleted preposition.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان بأن خسر قد جاء متعدياكقوله تعالى : ( خسروا أنفسهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes the loss concern the afterlife: failure to honor the balance leaves people losers on Judgment Day; al-Raghib says both worldly fairness and avoiding that loss are intended and interrelated.
rows.anchor: أي لا تخسروا أنفسكم في الميزان أي لا تكونوا خاسرين يوم القيامة بسبب الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account supplies an omitted noun for what is weighed, or uses “balance” figuratively for the weighed object.
rows.anchor: بتقدير مضاف أي موزون الميزان أو جعل الميزان مجازاعن الموزون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Haqqa may mean the Hour, an event whose occurrence must become real, a time in which true matters of reckoning and recompense are established, or a time when realities become known; Ibn Abbas transmits the last explanation.
rows.anchor: أي الساعة أو الحالة التي يحق ويجب وقوعها أو التي تحقق وتثبت فيها الأمور الحقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the last two senses the action is figuratively attributed to the Hour, properly belonging to the events or knowledgeable people within it; al-Kashf says this applies only to the final sense.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الفعل لها على الوجهين الأخيرين مجاز وهو حقيقة لما فيها من الأمور أو لمن فيها من أولي العلم

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the second sense may also be understood as a “possessor of realities” named after what accompanies it, and prefers this since the Hour and its contents are equally certain.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف كون الإسناد مجازيا إنما هو على الوجه الأخير

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari derives the name from overcoming an opponent in dispute: the Resurrection overcomes everyone who disputes God's religion falsely.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري الحاقة القيامة من حاقته فحققته أي غالبته فغلبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may be an adjective with its described noun omitted because the quality is unmistakable, a proper name for Judgment Day, or a verbal noun like “outcome”; in every case it begins the sentence whose predicate follows.
rows.anchor: وظاهر كلامهم أنها على جميع ذلك وصف حذف موصوفه للإيذان بكمال ظهور اتصافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question stresses the Hour's terror and magnitude: it lies beyond creatures' knowledge or imagination, and every estimate of its horror falls short.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لهولها وفظاعتها ببيان خروجها عن دائرة علوم المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative indirectly says that no awareness can reach or encompass it; the first “what” is a subject and “informed you” its predicate.
rows.anchor: ومنه يعلم أن الإستفهام كني به عن لازمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “what is the Hour?” is in the accusative after an elided preposition, suspended as an indirect question, rather than serving as a second object governed directly by “informed.”
rows.anchor: وما الحاقة جملة محلها النصب على إسقاط الخافض لا أن أدري يتعدى إلى المفعول الثاني بالباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question sentence as a whole coordinates with the preceding short clause.
rows.anchor: والجملة أعني ما أدراك الخ معطوفة على ما قبلها من الجملة الصغرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “the human” rather than using a pronoun emphasizes the material involved; because the verse says humanity came from a drop, it primarily means human descendants rather than Adam, or it uses the majority's material for the whole class.
rows.anchor: وفي إقامة الظاهر مقام المضمر فضل التقرير والتمكين في النفس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Reports from Qatada, al-Thawri, Ikrima, al-Shaʿbi, and Ibn Abbas say Adam is intended; Ibn Abbas says he lay between Mecca and Taif for forty years before receiving the spirit.
rows.anchor: ورويت إرادته عن قتادة والثوري وعكرمة والشعبي وابن عباس أيضا وقال في رواية أبي صالح عنه مرت به أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: In another report from Ibn Abbas through al-Dahhak, Adam was formed in stages: clay, dark mud, then molded clay, forty years each, and his form was complete after 120 years before the spirit was breathed into him.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية الضحاك عنه أنه خلق من طين فأقام أربعين سنة ثم من حمأ مسنون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi reports Ibn Abbas's view that the “time” was an extended period whose length is unknown; Ikrima similarly says no one knows how long passed before God created the human.
rows.anchor: وحكي الماوردي عنه أن الحين المذكور ههنا هو الزمن الطويل الممتد الذي لا يعرف مقداره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Sufis construe the opening question as denying any time when humans were not mentioned, implying the human species has existed for every time; Alusi calls this species-level eternity disbelief by consensus.
rows.anchor: وظاهره القول بقدم الإنسان في الزمان على معنى أنه لم يكن زمان إلا وفيه إنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An attempted defense says Ibn Arabi meant humanity's eternal archetype, not temporal existence: the Perfect Human makes divine knowledge visible when clothed in existence; Alusi counters that all things in immutable archetypes are eternal, not humanity alone.
rows.anchor: لو لم يكن في العالم من هو على صورة الحق ما حصل المقصود من العلم بالحق

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Alusi says leading Companions understood the verse affirmatively: Umar heard it recited and wished the phrase had been completed, showing he took it as a report of prior nonexistence.
rows.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وغيره عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه سمع رجلا يقرأ هل أتى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud likewise wished the verse completed; after he was rebuked, he picked up a clod and said he wished he were like it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه سمع رجلا يتلو ذلك فقال يا ليتها تمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshaj is parsed as a plural of several related forms meaning mixtures; its plural adjective modifies the singular drop because it contains multiple fluids or constituent parts and qualities.
rows.anchor: بالجمع وهي مفردة لأن بها مجموع ماء الرجل والمرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report distinguishes bodily contributions: male fluid contributes sinew, bone, and strength, while female fluid contributes flesh and blood.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار إنما كان من عصب وعظم وقوة فمن ماء الرجل وما كان من لحم ودم فمن ماء المرأة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari prefers treating amshaj as a singular pattern on afʿāl; the usual position of Sibawayh and most grammarians is that this pattern is not singular.
rows.anchor: واختاره الزمخشري والمشهور عن نص سيبويه وجمهور النحاة أن أفعالا لا يكون جمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most interpreters take the mixed drop to combine male and female fluids; another view mixes blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile, while a third treats amshaj itself as those four humors.
rows.anchor: نطفة مختلطة عند الأكثرين نطفة اختلط وامتزج فيها الماءان وقيل اختلط فيها الدم والبلغم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the drop has colors: male fluid is white, female fluid yellow, and after mixing and remaining in the womb it turns green, like water left to stand.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن مجاهد أنه قال أمشاج أي ألوان أي ذات ألوان

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets amshaj as the veins in the drop, an explanation also transmitted from Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: أخرج عن زيد بن أسلم أنه قال الأمشاج العروق التي في النطفة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima and Ibn Abbas interpret the mixtures as developmental stages from drop to clot to morsel through complete formation and the breathing of the spirit.
rows.anchor: وروي عكرمة وكذاابن عباس أنه قال أمشاج أطوار أي ذات أطوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Testing him” is a prospective circumstantial clause describing God's intention to test the human through later accountability, or figuratively the transfer from stage to stage, which answers why testing precedes becoming hearing and seeing.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى نبتليه حال من فاعل خلقنا والمراد مريدين ابتلاءه واختباره بالتكليف فيما بعد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ proposes fronting the clause: God made the human hearing and seeing in order to test him; Alusi calls this forced because the syntax and sense do not support the reversal.
rows.anchor: وقيل الكلام على التقديم والتأخير والجملة استئناف تعليلي أي فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the human hearing and seeing follows from the test's purpose: these faculties let him perceive signs in the world, himself, and revelation.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجعل كالمسبب عن الابتلاء لأن المقصود من جعله كذلك أن ينظر الآيات الآفاقية والأنفسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The independent explanatory clause says God showed the path through revealed evidence and rational signs in the world and within the self, after accountability and testing.
rows.anchor: أي دللناه على ما يوصله من الدلائل السمعية كالآيات التنزيلية والعقلية كالآيات الآفاقية والأنفسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thankful or ungrateful” may describe two states of the same person, since the path is shown in either state, or divide people: some follow truth gratefully and others reject it arrogantly.
rows.anchor: إما للتفصيل باعتبار تعدد الأحوال مع اتحاد الذات أي هديناه ودللناه على ما يوصل إلى البغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further grammatical possibility describes the two paths themselves as thankful and ungrateful by metonymy for their walkers.
rows.anchor: حالان من السبيل أي عرفناه السبيل إما سبيلا شاكرا وإما سبيلا كفورا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says “the path” means the route by which an infant exits the womb; Alusi rejects this as wholly untenable.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي أن السبيل هنا سبيل الخروج من الرحم وليس بشيء أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal and Abu al-Ajjaj read imma with an open initial vowel both times, a dialect form that some classify among conjunctions; a cited line of poetry attests the paired form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال وأبو العاج أما بفتح الهمزة في الموضعين وهي لغة حكاها أبو زيد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari construes the alternatives conditionally: gratitude comes by God's enabling, while disbelief comes from one's poor choice.
rows.anchor: وجعلها الزمخشري أما التفصيلية المتضمنة معنى الشرط على معنى أما شاكرا فبتوفيقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi finds that conditional gloss strained and favors taking the alternatives as different responses to God's guidance, which can apply to either outcome without making guidance the opposite of misguidance.
rows.anchor: وهذا التقدير إبراز من هلل ولا عليه أن يجعله من باب يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes the thankful person rewarded and the ungrateful punished; the emphatic form “ungrateful” also accommodates the rhyme and suggests ordinary people rarely escape some ingratitude.
rows.anchor: وجوز الانتصاف أن يكون أما شاكرا فمثاب وأما كفورا فمعاقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Woe is glossed as severe evil, grief, destruction, painful punishment, or a valley in Hell; a report attributed to Uthman reaches the Prophet but has a questionable chain.
rows.anchor: قيل الويل شدة الشر وقيل الحزن والهلاك وقيل العذاب الأليم وقيل في جهنم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet's description of Wail as a valley in Hell into which a disbeliever falls for forty years before reaching its bottom.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ويل واد في جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim give a version calling it a valley between two mountains; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Abdullah that it is a Hell valley.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيحي ابن حبان والحاكم بلفظ واد بين جبلين يهوي فيه الكافر

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says the word means shame or ugliness and can also express regret; al-Raghib cautions that the valley interpretation denotes the Hell abode deserved by those God calls wretched, not the dictionary meaning itself.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب المفردات للراغب قال الأصمعي ويل قبوح وقد يستعمل للتحسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether it literally names that valley or does so by another semantic relation requires examination; grammatically it can begin a sentence because it functions as a curse, with “to the defrauders” as predicate.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان فهو مبتدأ وإن كان نكرة لوقوعه في موقع الدعاء وللمطففين خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defrauding is shortchanging in measure or weight; the root suggests a tiny amount, while the intensive form indicates repeated acts rather than a large amount each time.
rows.anchor: والتطفيف البخس في الكيل والوزن لما أن ما يبخس في كيل أو وزن واحد شيء طفيف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives the word from the edge of a thing.
rows.anchor: وعن الزجاج أنه من طف الشيء جانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause can define which defrauders are meant or describe their characteristic conduct: when taking from people in a sale, they demand a full, generous measure.
rows.anchor: صفة مخصصة للمطففين الذين نزلت فيهم الآية أو صفة كاشفة لحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says “against people” reflects the grasping force of taking over; another says it marks harm to people, since they obtain full measure by compaction, shaking, and similar tricks.
rows.anchor: لتضمين الاكتيال معنى الاستيلاء أو للإشارة إلى أنه اكتيال مضر للناس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says min and ʿala interchange here: they take in full what is owed to them by others.
rows.anchor: فعن الفراء أن من وعلى يعتقبان في هذا الموضع فيقال اكتلت عليه أي أخذت ما عليه كيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reports objections: this gloss misses ordinary purchases from people to whom no debt is owed, and “taking in full” ordinarily means receiving one's due, so it alone does not explain the condemnation.
rows.anchor: مع اقتضائه لعدم شمول لاكتيالهم قبل أن يكون لهم على الناس شيء بطريق الشراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi answers that the paired conduct condemns them as in saying someone takes his due fully but gives others theirs short; this combination is blameworthy even if full receipt alone is proper.
rows.anchor: قلنا مدار الذم ما تضمنه مجموع المتعاطفين والكلام كقولك فلان يأخذ حقه من الناس تاما ويعطيهم حقهم ناقصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since a person's purchase from another usually concerns a due acquired through trade, al-Farraʾ may be describing the common case; the author invites consideration.
rows.anchor: ثم يقال إن الأغلب في اكتيال الشخص من شخص كون المكيل حقا له بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed focus reading takes “against people” with “they take in full,” meaning they do so only against others, not themselves; critics say taking fully from oneself is not a plausible contrast.
rows.anchor: وجوز على أن تكون على متعلقة بيستوفون ويكون تقديمها على الفعل لأفادة الخصوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its defenders paraphrase the focus as harming others but not themselves, since they take extra from buyers while taking less when selling; Alusi remains unconvinced.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن المراد بالاستيفاء المعدي بعلى على ذلك الإضرار فكأنه قيل إذا اكتالوا يضرون الناس خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detached pronoun refers to the people from whom they receive goods: when they measure or weigh for them in a sale, they give short measure or weight.
rows.anchor: والضمير المنفصل في قوله تعالى وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verb can mean measure for someone or measure that person's goods, some grammarians posit deletion of a preposition; poetry and a proverb illustrate such deletion, while another analysis supplies the omitted measured goods.
rows.anchor: وجعل غير واحد كاله من باب الحذف والإيصال على أن الأصل كال له فحذف الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isa ibn Umar and Hamza treat the pronoun as an emphatic subject following the verb's subject, pausing after the two waw letters to clarify that reading.
rows.anchor: وعن عيسى بن عمر وحمزة أن المكيل له والموزون له محذوف وهم ضمير مرفوع تأكيد للضمير المرفوع

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects reading the pronoun as subject: it would say they exact full measure when buying but cheat only when personally doing the measuring, an incoherent contrast because the passage concerns conduct, not who performs it.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري لا يصح كون الضمير مرفوعا للمطففين لأنه يكون المعنى عليه إذا أخذوا من الناس استوفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further objection says subject emphasis does not fit the context, which is not distinguishing them from their servants, and the expected consequence would have a connective fa; the detached-object reading also has support from the written form.
rows.anchor: لأن التأكيد اللفظي يدفعه المقام فليس المراد أن يحقق أن الكيل صدر منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They used measures to take goods because this allowed them to demand full amounts and cheat; when paying they used both measures and weights to shortchange in either way, so the verse mirrors their practice.
rows.anchor: إن المطففين كانوا لا يأخذون ما يكال ويوزن إلا بالمكاييل دون الموازين

rows.speaker: صبغة الله الحيدوي
rows.claim: Sayyid Sibghat Allah al-Haydawi argues that measurement cheating usually removes a negligible amount, whereas a small weighing trick can cost much more because weighed goods tend to be more valuable; mentioning cheating even in measures implies worse theft by weight.
rows.anchor: السيد صبغة الله الحيدوي في ذلك أنالتطفيف في الكيل يكون بشيء قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says this does not answer why the verse does not instead say they exact in measures and cheat by weight, which would imply the inverse by a fortiori reasoning; ellipsis could make that an instance of antimetabole-like omission.
rows.anchor: لا يحسم السؤال لجوازان يقال لم لم يقل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mentioning full measure stands for full weight as well, since buying and selling goods use both measures and weights; al-Tibi explains that one side of the parallel implies the other, which Alusi finds unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج المعنى إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل وكذلك إذا اتزنوا استوفوا الوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says these merchants buy large quantities at once, commonly measured, then sell smaller lots; sales vary in quantity and buyers choose weight or measure, so both are named when they give goods.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المطففين باعة وهم في الغلالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi cautions that buying large quantities by measure is not universal: in Baghdad of his day, people weighed everything and did not use measures.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن كون العادة الغالبة أخذ الكثير في الكيل غير مسلم على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other exegetes say neither statement specifies the commodity measured or weighed, because the passage condemns misconduct in taking and giving generally.
rows.anchor: وعدم التعرض للمكيل والموزون في الصورتين على ما قال غير واحد لأن مساق الكلام لبيان سوء معاملة المطففين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed question magnifies the enormity of their fraud: the initial hamza conveys denial and astonishment, joined to a negative la, rather than an introductory or attention-getting particle; “belief” retains its ordinary sense.
rows.anchor: استئناف وارد لتهويل ماما ارتكبوه من التطفيف والهمزة لإنكار والتعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” points to the defrauders, highlighting their defining vice and setting them apart; its distance suggests how far they are from goodness and corruption, so the question denies they believe in resurrection.
rows.anchor: ووضعه موضع ضميرهم للإشعار بمناط الحكم الذي هو وصفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is beyond measure in greatness; even weak belief in it would restrain such crimes, and it is called great because of what it contains. It is the cause of resurrection, though some supply “account of” before “day.”
rows.anchor: لا يقادر قدر عظمه فإن من يظن ذلك وإن كان ظنا ضعيفا لا يكاد يتجاسر على أمثال هذه القبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take “belief” here to mean certainty; Alusi considers the ordinary meaning more apt and eloquent.
rows.anchor: وقيل الظن هنا بمعنى اليقين والأول أولى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God portrays the defrauders as worse than other unbelievers, since others are at least described as having a weak supposition while this group is not.
rows.anchor: وعن الزمخشري أنه سبحانه جعلهم أسوأ حالا من الكفار لأنه أثبت جل شأنه للكفار ظنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi clarifies that the denial rhetorically treats them as people without even a weak belief, allowing the question to condemn them.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنه تعالى نزلهم منزلة من لا يظن ليصح الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanud means intensely ungrateful and rejecting blessings; a poem illustrates the term for one ungrateful to men's kindness.
rows.anchor: أى لكفور جحود من كند النعمة كفرها ولم يشكرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil report dialectal glosses: Kinda and Hadramawt use it for a sinner, Rabiʿa and Mudar for an ingrate, and Kinana for a miser and poor master, like barren land; al-Kalbi gives a similar account with Malik for miser.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومقاتل الكنود بلسان كندة وحضر موت العاصى وبلسان ربيعة ومضر الكفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most interpreters, including Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan, take it as ungrateful; a report from Abu Umama is attributed to the Prophet, and another report from al-Hasan describes blaming God, counting misfortunes, and forgetting blessings.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على تفسيره بالكفور وكل مما ذكر لايخلو عن كفران

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A weak Prophetic report from Abu Umama calls the ungrateful person one who beats a servant, withholds support, and eats alone; a parallel account is preserved as Abu Umama's own statement.
rows.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أبى امامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All reported meanings involve ingratitude, and extreme ingratitude gathers its different forms; “the human” is generic, but the judgment concerns some members of the class.
rows.anchor: والكفران المبلغ فيه يجمع صنوفا منه وال في الإنسان للجنس والحكم عليه بما ذكر باعتبار بعض الأفراد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view from Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about the specific unbeliever Qurt ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Nawfal; the following warning might support this, but Alusi doubts the identification.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به كافر معين لما روى عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في قرط بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: Isam al-Din prefers a universal reading: human nature tends to ingratitude unless God protects a person; this also praises warriors who strive against their natural inclination.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به كل الناس على معنى أن طبع الإنسان يجمله على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase “to his Lord” attaches to “ungrateful”; its fronting serves the rhyme despite being especially relevant to the blame for denying God's favors.
rows.anchor: ولربه متعلق بكنود واللام غير مانعة من ذلك وقدم للفاصلة
